comparator.name: Global Responsibility and Leadership
components: Entry requires completion of all foundation and Skills Lab courses. This 10 EC project brings students, academic supervisors and external partners together to frame a research question, analyse evidence and produce practical recommendations or another agreed output.
The minor semester can include an exchange, an internship or courses from another faculty.

The final 10 EC capstone combines supervised research (70%) with a personal and social-responsibility portfolio (30%). The portfolio develops across the degree; both parts count within the same 10 EC.

core: Environmental systems, climate, sustainable energy and human pressures
Political power, economic institutions, ethical responsibility and global justice
Culture, social inclusion, behaviour and population health
Interdisciplinary empirical research, responsible leadership and local-global inquiry
adjacent: Institutions, political economy and public accountability
questions: How can evidence from environment, social life and institutions support responsible local responses to global challenges?

alternatives.label: Interdisciplinary sustainability, governance and health
alternatives.concept: Connect environmental and energy processes with population health, social inclusion, culture, public institutions and ethical responsibility. Quantitative and qualitative methods, data analysis and stakeholder-focused inquiry give these domains a shared research basis. The programme responds to Groningen’s documented common academic core; it does not reproduce an unverified formal major, the full Living Lab or its thesis/portfolio culmination.

alternatives.label: Energy, climate and environmental resources
alternatives.concept: Investigate climate and energy transitions through Earth, soil and water systems, biodiversity, renewable energy and resource recovery. Field, laboratory, geospatial and statistical methods support environmental explanations; economics, justice and governance connect them to societal choices. This is a related environmental direction, not certification of Groningen’s unverified Energy, Ecology and Climate major.

alternatives.label: Politics, institutions and global responsibility

Empirical economics and qualitative methods support public argument and institutional analysis. This is a related political direction; the unknown formal-major allocation and its specialist depth are excluded.

selection.assessment: The broad closest programme already implements the evidenced culture/inclusion/health interests through population health, psychology, cultural representation and social inquiry. Test energy/environment next, then politics/institutions. Both provide genuine whole-programme priorities and exceed30ECdistinctness. Three programmes reached; no fourth formal-major lookalike is added. The older culture/health-only trial remains internal research, not an additional published programme.

trace: Planetary boundaries, chemical/thermodynamic/mechanical principles, models and a starch-biopolymer experiment provide a direct systems/physical-science foundation for environmental and energy questions; not the full five-sphere Earth course.
Supply/demand, consumer choice, production/costs, game theory and introductory macroeconomic markets directly support economic foundations, responsible-consumption and energy/policy trade-offs.

Networks, identity/boundaries and race/gender/migration/stratification provide actual concepts for social inclusion and unequal life opportunities. The library research is not a guaranteed community-health study.

Operationalisation, sampling, experimental/survey design, measurement quality, inference/regression and an R-based empirical project directly support interdisciplinary research. Specific GRL datasets or stakeholder projects are not guaranteed.

Actual interviews/focus groups, ethnography, documentary/visual methods, coding and reflexivity directly support research on communities/culture and stakeholder decisions; a project theme is not guaranteed.

Moral theories and argument evaluation supply ethical analysis of global responsibility, fairness and inclusion. The actual philosophical essay is not a guaranteed pandemic or public-health ethics project.

R cleaning/joining, tabular/spatial/text exploration, visualisation and a data project directly support research-data handling. GRL additionally teaches Python, QGIS, digital/AI literacy and security; these are not automatically reproduced.
Actual greenhouse forcing/feedbacks/tipping points, sea-level/ocean impacts, energy/carbon pathways, justice and stakeholder communication directly support climate-action and adaptation inquiry.

Epidemiological measures/design, bias/confounding/causality, determinants/inequalities, needs assessment/screening and a stakeholder-informed local project give a direct population-health contribution. It does not guarantee running GRL’s real-time community campaign.

Learning, social influence, personality, neural/psychological mechanisms and case/research appraisal support behavioural foundations for inclusion and health psychology; not an all-biomedical global-health foundation.

Legal traditions, public/private law, rights, justice and social change with case analysis/moot/legal-research work supply institutional and rights-based tools for governance and inclusion. It is not itself global-health training.

Institutions/power, collective action, food/water/energy/climate cases and stakeholder-policy matrices directly implement sustainability governance and policy feasibility; no particular health-policy or global-governance project guaranteed.
Public goods, externalities, efficiency/equity and expenditure, with health/welfare/social-insurance examples, provide specific policy-appraisal tools for governance and distributional choices.

IR/geopolitical theories, colonial/economic/climate cases and a UN SecurityCouncil simulation directly support international power and cooperation. In the culture/health plan this is a specific complementary governance framework, not global-health science.
Social cognition, influence, groups/prejudice/prosocial behaviour and a theory-guided study proposal directly implement social explanations of behaviour. The proposal is not a completed experiment.

Actual racial construction/power, marginalized/Indigenous media, participant observation, archives, documentary podcast and PhotoVoice give a substantive culture/race/reflexive interpretation contribution to inclusion. The American cultural-history focus is narrower than Groningen’s linguistics/anthropology diversity.

Actual health inequalities, biopsychosocial determinants, prevention/behaviour-change, chronic illness and culturally attentive interview practice give a substantive social-health contribution. Global health systems and population research require additional study.

Coactive persuasion/framing/cognitive shortcuts and actual sustainability communication implementation support public argument and local action. The documented projects concern circular lifestyles, not a guaranteed government/health campaign.

Actual renewable resource/generation assessment, conversion, grids, storage, demand and quantitative/Polysun/mini-grid work directly implement sustainable-energy systems; not merely a broad environmental elective.

The description supports OLS/GLS/IV, causal/predictive distinctions, t/F/LM tests, sampling distributions, MonteCarlo and an empirical Stata paper. These are actual inferential/model methods for energy-policy and social research; no guaranteed climate/health data.

Sources/responsibility, force/conflict, human rights, economic/environmental relations, self-determination and treaty compliance directly implement global legal accountability; actual legal-case/podcast work is not a specialist health-law programme.

Structural inequality, identity/colonial conflict, human rights, peacebuilding and transitional justice with interdisciplinary podcast/policy-brief methods support peace and inclusion. Its contribution is political/social, not clinical trauma therapy.

Actual environmental-humanities interpretation of visual/sound/digital media, scientific risk and public sustainability discourse supports the cultural-environmental bridge. Ecocritical argument is not a dedicated full anthropology or Earth-science sequence.

An actual external-advisor sustainability research project includes literature/question/design, investigation and partner-facing product/report. This supports the LivingLab educational function, with different topic, credit and entry structure; no guaranteed method or field technique.

Wave/observation methods, chemical analysis and material behaviour supply physical/chemical prerequisites for energy/resource practicals. Its greenwashing/campaign critique connects scientific evidence to sustainability claims.

The official description supports natural-hazard geoscience/risk analysis and adaptation, including droughts and toxic algae. Full consideration is given without inventing missing methods or a specialist climate-modelling assessment.

Calculus, optimisation, differential equations and numerical/dynamic-model implementation provide specific quantitative tools for environmental/energy processes. This is complementary mathematical preparation, not a promised energy-grid model.

Nature-based coastal/water infrastructure, ecological connectivity and intervention design connect ecosystem processes to local environmental solutions; actual Zeeland examples are not all global climate mitigation.

Actual organism diversity, phylogeny, ecological roles, identification/microscopy and biodiversity measurement supply the biological/ecological basis for environmental sustainability. No full ecosystem-process/field-ecology sequence is claimed.
Actual ArcGIS georeferencing, projections, spatial/surface analysis and remote-sensing/image processing directly support spatial environmental-change investigation and research-data tools.

Soil physical/chemical/biological properties, salinity, aquifer geophysics and actual field/lab surveys support environmental quality and water/resource appraisal. This is not a general policy or climate course.

Consumer decisions under uncertainty, cognitive limits, market power, externalities and regulation explain behavioural/market barriers to sustainable energy and public decisions; actual algebraic/graphical research appraisal is used.

Flood/freshwater/salinity/pollution processes and governance/law/justice connect physical delta risks to social adaptation choices; site-based appraisal is specific, not generic sustainability context.
Aqueous equilibria/speciation, carbonate/redox, adsorption/weathering and geochemical lab/modelling support contaminant/nutrient/resource processes and remediation; not all Earth-system modelling.

Solar-panel/e-waste recycling, metal recovery and plant/mycelial soil remediation with real chemical protocols and analysis directly implement circular resource/material questions. These are not electricity-generation technologies.

Rock/mineral/sediment, tectonic and geophysical processes plus field reconstruction directly support physical Earth-system understanding and environmental resource histories; the project is geological, not a climate-data capstone.

The description supports geoscience research on geothermal energy, CO2storage and nuclear-waste challenges through literature/class reports and professional-conference communication. No absent field experiment or numerical method inferred.

The description supports movement theory, EnvironmentalJusticeAtlas cases, feminist/anti-colonial/degrowth and environmental-peacebuilding perspectives. These directly support climate/social justice and civic action; no absent research method invented.
Classical/contemporary political thought, rights/authority and normative argument directly support the political-philosophy strand and ethical/global-governance questions.
Comparative institutions/democracy, actors/participation and empirical measurement/V-Dem research directly support accountable institutions and comparative political inquiry.

Growth, labour/financial markets, expectations, open-economy relations and fiscal/monetary models support political-economy and socioeconomic conditions of inclusion. It is a complementary economic explanation, not a health-economics course.

Positive-law human-rights systems, dignity/reproductive rights, protection/monitoring and normative critiques provide direct tools for peace/justice, gender and inclusion questions, not a guarantee of clinical/public-health qualification.

Industrialisation, nationalism/imperialism, wars, decolonisation and globalisation with historical-source/essay methods explain changing political-economic institutions and power. This specific historical function is complementary rather than a current-policy substitute.

Arguments/fallacies, debate/speech delivery and actual educational climate/community storytelling supply specific public-communication tools for accountable policy and social participation. It is complementary to political analysis, not a political-science substitute.

Constitutional institutions/federalism/rights and administrative participation/remedies/fairness support comparative governance and accountability through legal interpretation and a comparative-constitution project.

Military institutions/technology/strategy and historically contested Western dominance provide a specific conflict/power perspective; primary-source/strategic-text research is complementary to contemporary peacebuilding, not equivalent.
EU representation, agenda setting, interests and policy implementation with amendment coding/project evidence directly support institutional/political accountability.

Comparative imperial administration, ideology, economic/military power and legacies support analysis of global inequality and institutions, using historiography and source research; not a health or modern governance methods course.

EU competences, legal effect/liability/remedies, citizenship/free movement and digital/green-transition applications give specific supranational institutional/legal tools; not the same as EU political-process research.
blocks: Documented common core and related UCR study
Both develop reflection and personal learning. UCR adds scholarly literacy and community co-design; it does not reproduce the entire Groningen leadership and portfolio journey.

Environmental systems, human pressures and simple modelling overlap. UCR emphasizes physical/chemical sustainability tools; Groningen gives a broader Earth-system account. Climate Change and Dynamic Earth add related content elsewhere.
Both introduce markets, choice, production and macroeconomic questions. UCR uses algebraic and graphical analysis; neither relationship certifies the later major.
Both develop descriptive statistics, inference and research reasoning. UCR combines this with survey/experimental design and an R project.
Both teach qualitative research design, evidence collection and interpretation. UCR includes interviews, visual and documentary methods and coding; project settings may differ.
Both develop normative reasoning and critical ethical argument. UCR teaches general ethical theories; Groningen specifically frames global responsibility.
Both develop data handling for interdisciplinary research. UCR uses R; Groningen additionally specifies Python and QGIS, digital/AI literacy and security.

Both investigate population health and social/environmental determinants. UCR emphasizes epidemiological measures, evidence and needs assessment; Groningen additionally studies global structures/governance and community campaigns.
Both analyze international actors, power and cooperation. UCR uses international-relations theories and a UN simulation; Groningen frames global responsibilities through the SDGs.
Both study social cognition, influence and group behaviour. Groningen also introduces wider individual, cultural and environmental explanations.

Critical interpretation of race, representation, power and cross-cultural evidence supplies a cultural-analysis relationship. Groningen has a wider linguistics/anthropology approach; UCR is American cultural-history/media study.
Both investigate energy transitions and sustainable technologies. UCR adds yield/storage/grid calculations and system modelling; this is a partial relationship, not a formal major equivalence.

Both develop regression/inference, causal versus predictive reasoning and model assessment. UCR uses economic examples/Stata; Groningen additionally uses climate/energy/health data, uncertainty and risk.

Both involve partner-defined research, theory and method choice and a practical output. UCR is a 7.5-EC regional team research course with different entry requirements and timing; Groningen requires a 10-EC Living Lab after all foundation and Skills Lab courses.
Genuine 30-EC minor, exchange or internship space remains student-selected; no fixed UCR course counterpart.
Required 10-EC semi-independent thesis and degree-long responsibility portfolio remain unmatched. Course papers and policy reports or optional research do not establish equivalent culmination.

notes.text: This comparison covers Groningen’s confirmed interdisciplinary core. The 65 EC of unverified major/elective study are excluded. UCR’s related environmental and political directions do not certify an external major. Groningen also requires a 10-EC Living Lab and a 10-EC thesis/portfolio capstone; UCR community projects, research papers and optional independent research do not establish equivalent completion of those requirements.

audience.programmeDescription: Global Responsibility and Leadership at Campus Fryslân combines environmental, political, economic, cultural, behavioural and health perspectives on sustainable development. Students learn research methods and apply them through stakeholder inquiry and a thesis with a responsibility portfolio.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This academic-core comparison covers Groningen’s documented interdisciplinary foundations, research methods, responsible-leadership development, Living Lab and thesis/portfolio requirements. The separate 30-EC minor is identified as choice space; the unverified 65 EC of major/elective study are excluded. The UCR programmes are broader educational responses to this common core. They do not establish a match to an external formal major, equivalent research culmination or a complete Groningen degree pathway.
